## 固定收益開篇論點

6月23日美國公債收盤扭轉前一交易日的名目債券賣壓，且以前端反彈最為明顯，但聯邦公開市場委員會（FOMC）會議後實質利率上升所帶來的緊縮約束並未消退。2年期殖利率下跌8個基點至4.16%，10年期收於4.50%，2s10s利差擴大至34個基點。這波牛市趨陡顯示，投資人下修聯準會即將升息的時點溢價，但長端仍面臨偏高的實質殖利率門檻。

市場分化來自3條管道。全球半導體股重挫帶動避險買盤，原油同時下跌，減輕短期通膨衝擊。2年期美國公債標售需求強勁，進一步顯示主席Kevin Warsh首次發表鷹派談話後，政策敏感券種已跌至足以吸引買盤的價位。衍生性商品市場也傳達相同訊息：投資人開始質疑首次升息是否必須早在下次會議就登場，但仍保留較長期間內政策進一步收緊的預期。

美國經濟數據並不支持市場全面轉向鴿派。全國商業活動加速，主要由製造業帶動，但就業收縮，供應延誤仍然明顯。區域調查也呈現相似的多空交錯格局：當前活動改善，勞動需求轉弱，價格壓力則不一致。因此，名目債券上漲反映短期通膨尾端風險下降及避險需求增強，而非成長明確惡化，或市場已認定政策將重返寬鬆。

通膨連結市場則是這波行情的主要限制。長端名目殖利率小幅下滑，但實質殖利率反而上升，損益兩平通膨率則下降。油價走低後，投資人願意降低未來通膨補償，卻未下修持有存續期間所要求的實質報酬。前端領漲，是因進一步緊縮的時點更不確定；長端漲幅落後，則反映具限制性的實質利率環境依然存在。

信用市場也呈現融資可得性與融資價格之間的差異。SpaceX完成大規模首次債券融資，證明超大型科技業借款人仍可取得資金；但新券讓利、訂單簿由高峰縮減，以及投資人偏好風險最低的券次，都顯示市場承接相當審慎。整體投資級債總報酬受惠於美國公債殖利率下滑，高收益債券基金則小幅走弱。

因此，收盤走勢再次開啟聯準會會議後的存續期間支撐題材，但範圍比先前更窄。週一實質利率走高的解讀仍然成立，近乎平行上移的名目殖利率走勢則未能延續。股市壓力、能源價格下跌及標售需求，使支撐集中於短天期券種；實質殖利率堅挺、美元走強及企業債定價具選擇性，則使整體緊縮動能延續。

## 美國公債利率、聯準會定價、實質殖利率與殖利率曲線結構

美國公債漲勢在各年期之間極不均衡。2年期殖利率下跌8個基點至4.16%，5年期下跌2個基點至4.27%，10年期與30年期殖利率各下滑1個基點，分別至4.50%與4.94%。前端回落幅度超過週一的升幅，中段與長端殖利率則僅止穩。這種格局顯示，市場重新評估的是聯準會行動的預期時點，而非全面重定價長期成長或實質利率風險。

殖利率曲線斜率直接反映前端表現較佳。2s10s利差擴大7個基點至34個基點，2s30s也擴大7個基點至78個基點。2s5s10s蝶式利差上升5個基點至-12個基點，2s10s30s蝶式利差則上升7個基點至-10個基點。2項指標都顯示，當日行情消化了近期前端與中段的部分壓力，但超長債對漲勢的反應仍相對有限。

拉長比較期間，利率環境仍具限制性。過去1週，2年期與5年期殖利率均上升11個基點，10年期上升7個基點，30年期僅上升1個基點。過去1個月，2年期上升3個基點，5年期持平，10年期下降6個基點，30年期下降13個基點。近期政策利率預期仍處高檔；較遠期殖利率則更受惠於緊縮政策最終將抑制通膨與需求的預期。

通膨連結市場清楚區分通膨補償下降與實質緊縮約束延續。10年期抗通膨債券（TIPS）殖利率上升1個基點至2.29%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則下降2個基點至2.21%。5年期與7年期實質殖利率各上升2個基點，分別至2.03%與2.15%；20年期與30年期實質殖利率各上升1個基點。因此，10年期名目殖利率下滑主要由損益兩平通膨率下降帶動，實質殖利率仍維持在要求甚高的水準。

原油下跌使市場有明確理由調降通膨定價中的能源成分，但經濟數據使這股力量未能進一步壓低實質殖利率。美國標普全球綜合採購經理人指數（PMI）初值由51.5升至52.2，其中服務業為51.3、製造業為55.7，製造業產出指數更升至57.7。經濟活動加速意味著，僅憑油價走低仍不足以判定總體需求能否承受更高的政策利率路徑，甚至是否需要更高利率。

PMI內部細項使成長訊號更為複雜。就業連續第2個月下降，製造業人力以2020年以來最快速度收縮。供應商延誤為2022年8月以來最普遍，產出價格漲幅則維持在5月的高檔。勞動需求轉弱，支持聯準會耐心決定升息時點；但產能摩擦與定價壓力尚未消失，也使決策者仍須保持警戒。

區域數據進一步強化多空交錯的訊息。費城地區非製造業企業活動指數由-3.8改善至2.4，銷售指數由-7.6升至19.6；但全職就業指數降至-4.8，未來6個月企業展望也跌破零。支付價格指數降至25.8，收取價格指數則升至20.2。里奇蒙製造業綜合指數由13降至4，出貨、訂單及就業均轉弱，但企業回報的支付價格增速加快。

因此，利率市場降低了聯準會政策路徑中的急迫性，但並未排除進一步緊縮。利率交換市場盤中定價顯示，截至2027年年中累計升息幅度約45個基點，略低於先前水準，但仍超過1次25個基點的升息。關鍵差異在於政策順序：市場仍認為今年升息具有可能性，只是不再那麼確信首次行動必須立即到來。

選擇權交易更明確地反映市場對近期升息時點的質疑。聯準會決策公布後1日，擔保隔夜融資利率（SOFR）相關交易量倍增，許多部位押注升息次數少於整體貨幣市場定價。週一與週二合計投入近$3,000萬買進8月買權，以防債券上漲將10年期殖利率推低至4.4%或以下。現券市場調查也顯示，中性部位占比升至約2個月高點，反映市場仍充滿不確定性，而非已形成明確的鴿派共識。

美國財政部2年期公債標售把這種不確定性轉化為實際需求。這筆$690億標售的得標殖利率為4.189%，是2025年1月以來2年期公債標售的最高水準，且市場認為需求強勁。標售前，2年期券在FOMC會議後已明顯便宜化；標售結果進一步帶動前端在收盤前領漲。這證明市場願意接受當次標售條件，但5年期與7年期標售仍須檢驗相同買盤能否延伸至中段。

超短期融資也順利消化大額供給。$650億的42天期國庫券標售以3.620%的最高得標利率決標，投標倍數為2.91。獲配的競爭性投標中，間接投標人占65.67%、直接投標人占2.29%、交易商占32.04%；最高得標利率的配售比例為92.35%。該券於6月25日發行並交割，因此標售結果與後續現金移轉仍是兩項不同的流動性事件。

國庫券現券殖利率在這筆標售前後呈現分化。4週期券息等值殖利率下跌1個基點至3.62%，6週期殖利率則上升4個基點至3.69%。8週期殖利率下降1個基點至3.72%；13週期與17週期分別持平於3.79%及3.85%，26週期與52週期則降至3.95%及4.00%。6週期殖利率單獨上升，並未演變成前端融資利率普遍走高。

綜合而言，當日利率行情是在政策仍具限制性的環境內修正升息時點預期。2年期標售與避險需求，帶動FOMC會議後調整幅度最大的券種反彈。損益兩平通膨率下降，把油價走低傳導至名目殖利率；實質殖利率上升及價格數據多空交錯，則使這波漲勢未演變成市場全面否定Warsh的政策反應函數。因此，殖利率曲線趨陡反映市場對立即升息的信心下降，而非認定緊縮辯論已經結束。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

整體信用市場依存續期間與信用風險分化。隨著美國公債殖利率下滑，LQD上漲0.1195%；HYG下跌0.0876%，JNK下跌0.0519%。投資級債總報酬獲得溫和的利率助益；投機級債券基金小幅下跌，則顯示股市賣壓抑制風險偏好。這種表現不及全面風險偏好升溫，但距離融資普遍撤退仍相當遙遠。

SpaceX帶來關鍵的初級市場考驗。該公司首次發債募得$250億，高於前一交易日至少$200億的行銷規模。交易順利完成，解答了單一AI與基礎建設相關借款人能否消化如此龐大發債規模的眼前疑問。市場關注焦點也由能否取得融資，轉向投資人承擔風險所要求的補償及交易結構。

2036年到期債券的利差定為較美國公債高1.4個百分點，約比同評級BBB債券的平均利差寬0.4個百分點。這項新券讓利顯示，投資級評等與龐大股權價值仍不足以消除市場對現金流創造能力的疑慮。債券持有人取得合約約定的本息，卻無法充分分享衛星、人工智慧或太空資料中心的潛在上行利益，因此發行利差必須補償公司積極支出及執行計畫的風險。

訂單簿變化進一步凸顯投資人的審慎態度。需求高峰接近$900億，到定價時降至$730億。最終訂單簿不到發行金額的3倍，低於今年投資級債交易接近4倍的平均水準。投資人對天期最短、風險最低的券次需求最強。市場確有大額需求，但隨發行利差收窄、存續期間拉長，投資人也更加挑剔。

SpaceX的資產負債表在風險之外提供實質保障。截至6月19日，公司持有超過$1,000億現金，並表明有意維持投資級評等。評等機構指出，如有必要，公司可削減投資或增發股權。另一方面，S&P預期現金消耗將持續至2030年，且明年支出增速超過營收後，現金消耗將大幅加快。最終債券定價同時反映現有流動性，以及距離產生自由現金流仍有漫長路程。

指標利率避險使這筆交易直接影響美國公債。即使油價下跌，5年期與10年期殖利率週一仍升至至少1週高點，市場人士認為部分漲幅與這筆大型交易的利率避險有關。融資完成定價、2年期標售也順利結束後，市場不再需要承擔部分供給相關壓力。當日美國公債漲勢不只是單一交易避險部位解除，但發債完成確實移除了中段一項可辨識的負擔。

SpaceX股價也在連續3個交易日下跌後回升，凸顯股票的選擇權價值與債券持有人報酬結構的差異。股價止穩並未消除信用讓利，因為兩類投資人的損益結構不同。債券投資人著重現金流、到期償付及下檔保護；股票投資人則仍可參與公司最積極的成長情境。這項差異說明，成功完成融資與審慎的債券定價可以同時存在。

因此，初級市場承接能力深厚，但對價格相當敏感。投資人願意為規模極大的新借款人提供資金，卻要求利差寬於可比BBB債券；最終訂單簿也由高峰縮減，需求並集中於較短天期券種。結果延續前一交易日的結論：信用融資管道仍然暢通，但SpaceX供給的實際消化情況，比最高訂單金額所暗示的更具選擇性。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

已開發市場債券同時面對經濟活動訊號轉弱，以及央行不願宣告通膨衝擊已受控制。歐元區綜合PMI初值由48.5改善至49.5，但仍連續第3個月低於50。服務業指數升至48.9，製造業指數降至51.3，就業則小幅下滑。投入成本漲幅降至2月以來最低，銷售價格漲幅也降至3個月低點，對存續期間行情提供些許邊際支撐。

歐洲央行的談話限制了這項支撐。副總裁Boris Vujcic為6月升息25個基點辯護，理由是整體與核心通膨預計到2027年仍將高於目標。目前歐元區通膨率為3.2%。即使中東外交持續推進，首席經濟學家Philip Lane也警告，物價漲幅仍可能在一段時間內超過2%目標。因此，成長較溫和並不等同貨幣政策即將逆轉。

重要的制衡因素是，目前尚未出現廣泛的第二輪效應。Vujcic表示，平均每名員工薪酬正在下降，薪資並未產生擴散效應，中長期通膨預期也維持穩定。總裁Christine Lagarde先前亦認為，現階段無須採取更強力的政策回應。歐洲央行可以在政策維持限制性的同時，觀察薪資與通膨預期，再決定是否有必要再次升息；歐洲前端利率因而仍會對每一項通膨與經濟活動數據保持敏感。歐洲議會經濟委員會就數位歐元談判立場達成協議，使市場基礎設施另向前一步。方案保留現金的法定支付地位，同時推動12個月零售試行，並平行發展批發型央行數位貨幣。發行日期、持有上限及對存款的替代程度均未確定，因此當日沒有改變銀行融資。對固定收益市場而言，長期意義在於歐元支付、結算流動性，以及與主要以美元計價的穩定幣競爭所需的架構。

日本則透過標售需求與匯率呈現不同的存續期間限制。5年期日本公債（JGB）標售投標倍數為3.11，低於前次的3.22，也低於過去12個月平均的3.47。標售尾差由0.04擴大至0.06，期貨在結果公布後收斂漲幅。日圓貶破每美元160日圓，使輸入性通膨及日本央行加速緊縮的風險仍受關注，標售需求因而偏弱。

這次標售結果並不代表日本央行即將加快緊縮。隔夜指數交換市場定價顯示，今年剩餘期間的升息幅度不到額外1次25個基點，油價走低也減輕部分通膨壓力。即使如此，疲弱的5年期標售仍提高日本公債的市場承接門檻。當日本投資人在匯率不確定的環境下可取得更高的國內殖利率，經匯率避險後的海外債券便須與更具吸引力的本國市場替代選項競爭。

匈牙利顯示，匯率表現可創造逆全球緊縮趨勢而行的政策空間。福林先前升值改善通膨展望後，匈牙利央行將基準利率下調25個基點至6%。平均年通膨率預測現已降至1.8%，低於3月預估的3.8%。決策公布後，福林兌歐元一度下跌1.3%，反映投資人開始定價進一步寬鬆空間，也顯示運用這項政策空間須付出匯率代價。

財政與監理問題則為美國公債買方基礎帶來一項發展較緩慢的風險。Kiel Institute研究估計，若歐洲銀行與保險公司持有的美國政府債務適用20%的監理風險權數，未來10年歐洲對美國公債的需求可能減少約$2,000億，美國每年財政成本最多可能增加$420億。這只是分析情境，並非已實施的政策，因此未主導當日行情；但研究點出，監理待遇可能如何把地緣政治緊張傳導至期限溢價及聯邦政府融資成本。

全球利率環境仍不同步。歐元區上游價格壓力放緩，但歐洲央行仍審慎；日本公債標售需求疲弱，但市場僅預期日本央行漸進緊縮；匈牙利則因先前匯率走強改變通膨路徑而得以降息。這些差異使全球無法形成一致的存續期間動能。對美國公債而言，海外投資人要求的承接殖利率仍偏高且不均，這也有助解釋美國長端為何落後於前端漲勢。台灣在2%政策利率之下，另有金融穩定限制。股票融資餘額12個月增加160%，券商年內為支應營運資金已發行近$12億債券，股票交易違約金額6月也增加逾1倍至超過NT$20億。槓桿需求甚至是6月3日央行債券標售未足額承銷的因素之一。不過，違約仍不到整體交易的0.002%，截至5月，34家經營各類融資業務的券商也都沒有超越監管上限，因此尚不足以證明系統失靈。這些數據仍顯示，AI帶動的股市榮景可能把銀行與券商資產負債表由低風險資產移開，並使劇烈修正傳導至家庭消費、融資成本及本地債券需求。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

即使美國公債殖利率下滑，新興市場債仍面臨美元走強的壓力。EMB下跌0.1452%，美元指數上漲0.3861%至101.41。基金僅溫和下跌，顯示指標殖利率下降抵銷了部分美元環境收緊的影響，但並未重現LQD所獲得的投資級債利率助益。對外匯存底薄弱、進口支出龐大或近期有再融資需求的外部借款人而言，美元走強仍是更棘手的壓力來源。

伊朗可能取回遭凍結資金，凸顯釋放流動性與取得不受限制融資之間的差異。一名伊朗官員表示，$120億資金即將分2筆等額釋出，但美國尚未確認這項金額。美國總統Donald Trump表示，任何獲釋資金只能用於向美國購買食品與醫療用品。這項安排可支應必要進口，但用途限制也會降低資金支付其他外部債務的彈性。

同一外交進程仍使荷姆茲海峽的貿易條件存在不確定性。伊朗與阿曼表示，雙方將開始擬定管理該水道的協議，並承諾維持海峽安全與開放。通行成本仍待協商，市場也擔心未來可能徵收通行費。海峽持續安全開放，有利油價正常化及進口國外部收支；若通行成本偏高，即使未再發生軍事干擾，運費與能源價格壓力仍可能延續。

塞內加爾則帶來更直接的債務管理警訊。一名資深內閣部長表示，付款壓力持續升高並威脅重要經濟部門，該國願意考慮債務重整。目前尚未確立任何交易條款，因此這項發展只代表政府願意研議調整債務負擔，而非重整已經完成。儘管如此，這仍顯示經濟部門承受的壓力，可能使主權國家由例行融資轉向與債權人協商還款時點及負擔。Raizen則提供直接影響回收價值的企業重整更新。IG4 Capital表示，在約650億雷亞爾，折合$128億的債務中，45%轉為公司約80%股權後，該公司有足夠資本以全現金收購債權，並尋求取得50.1%股權。債權人可選擇現金、基金單位，或與未來出售連結的衍生工具；IG4可在明年3月前累積債權。提案仍在初步階段，各業務價值分配也未確定，但現金能力使控制權方案比單純附條件的出價更具可執行性。

這些案例凸顯強勢美元環境下各國處境分化。伊朗可能透過外交取得用途受限的外部資金；塞內加爾則因付款壓力已干擾國內經濟，而考慮改變債務條件。整體新興市場債僅小幅下跌，掩蓋了兩者的重大差異。各國取得美元流動性的條件高度不同，主權債結果取決於資金的法定用途、債權人條件，以及維持對外付款對國內經濟造成的成本。土耳其顯示高carry准入的報酬與脆弱性。外匯carry部位回升至約$300億，外資本幣債持倉增至約$150億，最近1週至少流入$60億carry資金。里拉1個月與3個月隱含殖利率降至32%及35%，央行則以40%向銀行提供資金，並估計買進約$90億外匯。資金流入有助重建準備金與需求，但仍容易因地緣政治升級或本地融資利率過早下降而逆轉。

摩洛哥利用食品通膨下降延長政策暫停，把利率維持在2.25%；5月通膨降至1.2%，農業改善與基礎建設支出則支撐2021年以來最快成長。不過，經常帳赤字預測上調至2026年GDP的4%、2027年的3.8%，仍構成外部平衡限制。巴西6月會議紀錄則呈現相反的公信力問題：央行連續第3次降息25個基點至14.25%後，整體與基礎通膨仍進一步偏離3%目標，決策者並暗示可能調整寬鬆幅度。兩者共同區分由通膨下降所取得的政策空間，以及可能跑在通膨預測前面的寬鬆。

## 跨資產

股市為美國公債帶來最明確的避險買盤。S&P 500下跌1.4363%，Nasdaq 100下跌3.2946%，半導體指數重挫7.8731%。半導體指數先前漲勢異常強勁，即使當日大跌，過去1個月仍上漲10.4894%。因此，當日走勢更像是AI領漲族群的集中性部位調整，而非市場全面下修經濟前景。賣壓集中於特定族群，也有助解釋美國公債買盤為何以政策敏感年期最為強勁。

波動率上升，但尚未達到失序水準。VIX上漲12.7893%至19.49。投資人增加避險部位，與美國公債殖利率下滑及美元走強一致，但VIX水準並未顯示系統性融資事件。即使晶片股遭到拋售，SpaceX股價仍自先前跌勢中回升，再次顯示股市衝擊雖大，卻未均勻波及整個科技產業。

油價下跌進一步壓低通膨補償。西德州原油（WTI）下跌2.1518%至$73.21，布蘭特原油下跌1.0526%至$77.08，兩者過去1個月均下跌逾24%。單日跌幅減輕能源價格對整體通膨的即時推力，較長期間的跌勢則強化損益兩平通膨率下滑的理由。不過，荷姆茲海峽管理方式仍在協商，這項通膨利多能否延續仍有變數。

美元走勢使單純的避險解讀更為複雜。美元指數升至101.41，當日上漲0.3861%，過去1週上漲1.8786%。避險需求是推力之一，但美元上漲也反映聯準會立場仍偏鷹派，而其他國家的政策前景較為分歧。只要投資人質疑的是下一次升息的時點，而非放棄美國的相對利率優勢，美國公債前端上漲就能與美元融資環境收緊並存。

儘管股市遭到拋售，黃金仍下跌1.2435%至$4,129.8999。黃金過去1週下跌4.6411%，過去1個月下跌8.6507%。金價疲弱與美元走強及實質殖利率高企一致，顯示股市衝擊並未充分帶動通膨或地緣政治避險需求，無法抵銷持有黃金的機會成本。

因此，跨資產市場分別強化固定收益論點的不同環節。股市下跌與波動率上升帶來避險需求；原油下跌壓低損益兩平通膨率；美元走強與黃金下跌則顯示，實質利率及相對政策環境仍具限制性。整體訊息符合由政策時點調整與風險部位縮減所推動的美國公債牛市趨陡，而非市場全面下修名目或實質利率路徑。

## 市場前瞻意義

6月25日美東時間8:30公布的美國數據，以5月個人所得與支出為主，將決定前端漲勢能否與FOMC會議後的實質利率重定價並存。4月核心個人消費支出（PCE）物價月增0.2%，整體PCE物價月增0.4%，支出增加0.5%，所得持平；初領失業救濟金人數、耐久財訂單及第1季國內生產毛額（GDP）第3次估值也將同時公布。若基礎通膨放緩、支出動能轉弱，且勞動市場進一步降溫，尤其損益兩平通膨率仍受控制，將確認6月23日市場已降低聯準會下一步行動的急迫性，並可能使債市漲勢由2年期延伸至10年期。若核心價格上漲範圍再次擴大、家庭需求維持韌性，或供應鏈壓力重現，則會削弱這項解讀、推升實質殖利率，並使市場重新評估Warsh較具限制性的政策反應函數是否要求更早升息。

6月24日，美國公債供給將移向中段。財政部將於美東時間13:00標售$700億5年期公債，此前於11:30進行$280億2年期浮動利率債增額發行及119天期國庫券標售。6月25日則將於13:00標售$440億7年期公債，並於11:30標售4週期與8週期國庫券；附息債券於6月30日交割，因此標售與後續現金移轉仍是不同事件。若投標倍數強勁、直接與間接投標人廣泛參與、交易商承接比例受控，且國庫券現券殖利率穩定，將延續2年期標售的強勁結果，並支持SpaceX避險壓力消退後，中段足以承接政府供給的觀點。若5年期或7年期需求疲弱、交易商承接比例偏高，或5年期實質殖利率再度上升，則供給溢價可能重現，並挑戰週二漲勢所反映的融資秩序仍然穩定這項判斷。

國際市場的承接殖利率考驗，將由6月24日雪梨時間11:30公布的澳洲5月消費者物價指數（CPI）揭開序幕，接著是6月25日東京時間約12:35進行、規模約¥7,000億的日本20年期公債增額發行，以及當日美東時間15:00的墨西哥央行利率決策。澳洲前期通膨數據為月增0.4%、年增4.2%；若價格上漲範圍縮小且匯率趨穩，將減輕再次緊縮的壓力，並降低區域實質利率底部。若日本公債投標倍數強勁、終端投資人需求穩健，將緩和5年期標售疲弱所引發的買方基礎疑慮；若標售尾差擴大或投標倍數下降，則會加劇全球長存續期間資產爭取資金的壓力。墨西哥央行目前政策利率為6.50%。若利率維持不變且披索穩定，將顯示油價下跌與政策可信度足以抑制美元壓力；若匯率壓力再起或政策指引轉趨緊縮，則會凸顯強勢美元的限制，並削弱市場對EMB小幅下跌的良性解讀。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The June 23 Treasury close reversed the previous session’s nominal selloff most clearly at the front end, without erasing the post-FOMC rise in real-rate restraint. The 2-year yield closed at 4.16% after an 8-basis-point decline, while the 10-year finished at 4.50% and the 2s10s curve widened to 34 basis points. That bull steepening showed investors trimming the timing premium for an imminent Fed increase, even as the long end retained a high real-yield hurdle.

3 channels produced that split. A global semiconductor rout created a haven bid just as falling crude reduced the immediate inflation impulse. Strong demand at the 2-year Treasury auction then reinforced the view that the policy-sensitive sector had cheapened enough after Chair Kevin Warsh’s hawkish debut. Derivatives activity pointed in the same direction: investors questioned whether a hike had to arrive as soon as the next meeting while preserving expectations of tighter policy over a longer horizon.

The domestic data did not validate a broad dovish turn. National business activity accelerated, led by manufacturing, yet employment contracted and supply delays remained pronounced. Regional surveys showed a similar mixture of current activity, weaker labor demand and uneven price pressure. The nominal rally therefore reflected a lower near-term inflation tail and greater demand for safety, not a clean deterioration in growth or a settled return to easing.

Inflation-linked pricing imposed the main qualification. The long nominal yield edged lower even as its real component rose and breakeven inflation fell. Investors were willing to reduce compensation for future inflation as oil declined, but they did not lower the real return required to hold duration. The front end led because the timing of additional restraint looked less certain; the long end lagged because the restrictive real-rate regime remained intact.

Credit markets delivered the same distinction between access and price. SpaceX completed its jumbo debut bond financing, proving that a very large technology borrower could obtain funds, but the concession, the shortening of the orderbook and the preference for the least risky tranche showed disciplined absorption. Broad high-grade total returns benefited from lower Treasury yields, while high-yield funds softened slightly.

The close thus reopened the duration-relief theme seen after the Fed meeting, but in a narrower form than before. Monday’s higher-real-rate interpretation survived, whereas its near-parallel nominal selloff did not. Equity stress, cheaper energy and auction demand shifted relief toward short maturities; firm real yields, a stronger dollar and selective corporate pricing kept the broader tightening impulse alive.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

The Treasury rally was highly uneven by maturity. The 2-year yield fell 8 basis points to 4.16%, the 5-year declined 2 to 4.27%, and the 10- and 30-year yields each slipped 1 basis point, to 4.50% and 4.94%. The front end recovered more than Monday’s increase, while intermediate and long yields merely stabilized. That pattern located the reassessment in the expected timing of Fed action rather than in a wholesale repricing of long-run growth or real-rate risk.

Curve slopes recorded the front-end outperformance directly. The 2s10s spread widened 7 basis points to 34, and 2s30s widened by the same amount to 78. The 2s5s10s butterfly rose 5 basis points to -12, while the 2s10s30s butterfly rose 7 to -10. Both measures show that the session unwound part of the recent front-end and belly pressure while leaving the long bond relatively resistant to the rally.

The longer comparison still describes a restrictive regime. Over 1 week, 2- and 5-year yields were each 11 basis points higher, the 10-year was 7 higher and the 30-year only 1 higher. Over 1 month, the 2-year was 3 basis points higher, the 5-year unchanged, the 10-year 6 lower and the 30-year 13 lower. Near-term policy expectations remain elevated, while distant yields continue to benefit more from the prospect that tighter policy eventually limits inflation and demand.

Inflation-linked markets separated falling inflation compensation from persistent real restraint. The 10-year TIPS yield rose 1 basis point to 2.29%, while the 10-year breakeven fell 2 basis points to 2.21%. 5- and 7-year real yields each increased 2 basis points, to 2.03% and 2.15%, and 20- and 30-year real yields each added 1. The nominal rally was therefore carried by lower breakevens at 10 years even as real yields stayed at demanding levels.

Crude’s decline offered a clear reason to reduce the energy component of inflation pricing, but the data prevented that move from spreading into lower real yields. The national flash composite PMI rose to 52.2 from 51.5, with services at 51.3 and manufacturing at 55.7. Manufacturing output strengthened to 57.7. Faster activity meant lower oil alone was insufficient to settle whether aggregate demand can tolerate, or require, a higher policy path.

The internal PMI details complicated the growth signal. Employment fell for a 2nd month, and factory headcount contracted at the sharpest pace since 2020. Supplier delays were the most widespread since August 2022, while output-price inflation remained at May’s elevated pace. These details support patience on the timing of a hike because labor demand is softening, yet they preserve the case for vigilance because capacity frictions and pricing pressure have not disappeared.

Regional releases reinforced that two-sided message. Philadelphia-area nonmanufacturing firm activity improved to 2.4 from -3.8 and sales rose to 19.6 from -7.6, but full-time employment fell to -4.8 and the 6-month firm outlook dropped below zero. Prices paid eased to 25.8 as prices received rose to 20.2. The Richmond manufacturing composite fell to 4 from 13, with weaker shipments, orders and employment, even as firms reported faster growth in prices paid.

Rates markets consequently reduced the amount of urgency embedded in the Fed path without discarding tightening. Swaps during the session priced about 45 basis points of increases by mid-2027, slightly less than before. That still represents more than 25 bp move. The distinction lies in sequence: the market continued to treat higher rates this year as plausible, but became less convinced that the 1st move must arrive immediately.

Options flows made the challenge to near-term timing more explicit. SOFR-linked trading volume doubled in the day after the Fed decision, with many positions favoring fewer increases than broader money markets implied. Nearly $30 million was spent over Monday and Tuesday on August calls protecting against a rally that could pull the 10-year yield toward 4.4% or below. Cash-market surveys also showed neutral positions at their highest in about 2 months, indicating uncertainty rather than a decisive dovish consensus.

Treasury’s 2-year sale converted that uncertainty into observable demand. The $69 billion auction stopped at 4.189%, the highest yield for a 2-year offering since January 2025, and was described as drawing strong demand. The result followed the sharp post-FOMC cheapening and helped the front end outperform into the close. It established demand at the auction terms; the 5- and 7-year sales still had to test whether the same appetite extends into the belly.

Very short funding also cleared in size. The $65.000 billion 42-day bill auction stopped at a 3.620% high rate with a 2.91 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders took 65.67% of accepted competitive tenders, direct bidders 2.29% and dealers 32.04%; 92.35% was allotted at the high. The security issues and settles on June 25, so the bidding result and the later cash transfer remain separate liquidity events.

Cash-bill yields showed differentiation around that sale. The 4-week coupon-equivalent yield fell 1 basis point to 3.62%, while the 6-week yield rose 4 to 3.69%. 8 weeks declined 1 basis point to 3.72%; 13- and 17-week yields were unchanged at 3.79% and 3.85%, and 26- and 52-week yields fell to 3.95% and 4.00%. The isolated 6-week increase did not become a common front-end funding move.

Taken together, the rates close was a timing correction inside a still-restrictive policy regime. The 2-year auction and safety demand rewarded the sector that had borne the greatest post-FOMC adjustment. Falling breakevens transmitted cheaper oil into nominal yields, while rising real yields and mixed price data prevented the rally from becoming a broad rejection of Warsh’s reaction function. The steepening therefore reflects less confidence in an immediate hike, not confidence that the tightening debate is finished.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

The broad credit tape split along duration and risk lines. LQD gained 0.1195% as Treasury yields fell, while HYG declined 0.0876% and JNK slipped 0.0519%. High-grade total returns received a modest rate benefit; the small losses in speculative-grade funds showed that the equity selloff restrained risk appetite. The combination was softer than a full risk-on response, yet far from a generalized withdrawal of financing.

SpaceX supplied the decisive primary-market test. The company raised $25 billion in its debut bond financing after marketing a transaction of at least $20 billion in the prior session. Completion resolved the immediate question of whether a single AI- and infrastructure-linked borrower could clear a deal of that scale. It also transferred the debate from simple market access to the compensation and structure required for investors to absorb the risk.

The 2036 bonds priced at a spread of 1.4 percentage points over Treasuries, roughly 0.4 percentage point wider than the average for similarly rated BBB debt. That concession showed that investment-grade ratings and a very large equity value did not eliminate concern over cash generation. Bondholders receive contractual payments without sharing fully in the upside from satellites, artificial intelligence or space-based data centers, so the clearing spread had to compensate for ambitious spending and execution risk.

Orderbook behavior sharpened the message. Demand approached $90 billion at the peak, then fell to $73 billion by pricing. The final book was less than 3 times the amount sold, below an average near 4 times for high-grade transactions this year. Investors showed the strongest appetite for the shortest and least risky tranche. Large demand was real, but it became more selective as pricing tightened and duration extended.

The balance sheet provided meaningful protection alongside the risk. SpaceX held more than $100 billion of cash as of June 19 and has stated an intention to preserve high-grade ratings. Rating firms indicated that investment could be reduced or additional equity raised if necessary. Against that, S&P expected cash burn to continue through 2030 and accelerate sharply next year as spending grows faster than revenue. The bond outcome priced both liquidity and the long runway before free cash generation.

Benchmark-rate hedging linked the transaction directly to Treasuries. 5- and 10-year yields had reached at least 1-week highs on Monday even as oil declined, with market participants associating part of that move with hedging for the jumbo deal. Once the financing priced and the 2-year auction cleared, some of that supply-related pressure no longer needed to be carried. The day’s rate rally was broader than a deal unwind, but completed issuance removed one identifiable burden from the belly.

SpaceX shares also recovered from a 3-session selloff, underscoring the difference between equity optionality and bondholder economics. The stock’s stabilization did not erase the credit concession, because the 2 investor groups face different payoff structures. Debt investors emphasized cash flow, maturity and downside protection; equity investors retained exposure to the company’s most ambitious growth scenarios. The contrast helps explain why a successful financing and cautious bond pricing coexisted.

Primary absorption was therefore deep and price-sensitive. Investors funded an exceptionally large new borrower, but required a wider spread than comparable BBB debt, allowed the final book to shrink and concentrated demand in shorter maturities. The result continued the prior session’s conclusion that credit access remains open, while resolving the prospective SpaceX supply question in a more discriminating form than the strongest headline order figure suggested.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Developed-market duration faced a split between softer activity signals and central banks unwilling to declare the inflation shock contained. Euro-area flash PMI improved to 49.5 from 48.5, yet remained below 50 for a 3rd month. Services rose to 48.9, manufacturing eased to 51.3 and employment fell fractionally. Input-cost inflation slowed to its weakest since February, and selling-price inflation was the softest in 3 months, offering duration some relief at the margin.

ECB communication limited that relief. Vice President Boris Vujcic defended the June quarter-point increase because headline and core inflation are expected to remain above target into 2027. Current euro-area inflation stood at 3.2%. Chief Economist Philip Lane likewise warned that price growth may exceed the 2% goal for some time even as Middle East diplomacy progresses. A milder growth outcome therefore did not amount to a policy reversal.

The important counterweight was the absence of a broad second-round process. Vujcic said compensation per employee was falling, wages did not show ripple effects and medium- to long-term inflation expectations remained anchored. President Christine Lagarde had also seen no need for a more forceful response at this stage. The ECB can keep policy restrictive while waiting for wages and expectations to determine whether another increase is necessary, leaving European front ends sensitive to each inflation and activity release. The digital euro cleared a separate market-infrastructure step when the European Parliament's economic committee agreed on its negotiating position. The plan preserved cash as legal tender while advancing a 12-month retail pilot and parallel work on wholesale central-bank digital money. No issuance date, holding limit or deposit displacement was established, so it did not alter bank funding that day. Its fixed-income relevance lies in the future architecture of euro payments, settlement liquidity and competition with predominantly dollar-based stablecoins.

Japan presented a different duration constraint through auction demand and the currency. The 5-year JGB sale produced a 3.11 bid-to-cover ratio, down from 3.22 previously and below the 12-month average of 3.47. The auction tail widened to 0.06 from 0.04, and futures trimmed gains after the result. Demand was subdued as the yen’s move beyond 160 per dollar kept imported-inflation and faster-BOJ-tightening risks in view.

The Japanese result did not imply an imminent acceleration in policy. Overnight swaps priced less than one additional 25-basis-point increase for the rest of the year, and lower oil reduced part of the inflation pressure. Even so, a weak 5-year auction raises the domestic clearing hurdle for sovereign duration. When Japanese investors can obtain higher local yields amid currency uncertainty, hedged foreign bonds must compete with a more demanding home-market alternative.

Hungary demonstrated that currency performance can create room to move against the global tightening tilt. The central bank cut its benchmark by 25 basis points to 6% after the forint’s prior appreciation improved the inflation outlook. Average annual inflation is now projected at 1.8%, down from a 3.8% forecast in March. The forint fell as much as 1.3% against the euro after the decision as investors priced scope for further easing, showing the exchange-rate cost of using that policy room.

Fiscal and regulatory questions added a slower-moving Treasury buyer-base risk. A Kiel Institute study estimated that applying a 20% regulatory risk weight to US government debt held by European banks and insurers could reduce regional Treasury demand by about $200 billion over a decade and add as much as $42 billion a year to US fiscal costs. The scenario was analytical, not an enacted policy, so it did not drive the close. It nevertheless identifies how regulatory treatment could transmit geopolitical tension into term premium and federal financing costs.

The global map remains asynchronous. Softer euro-area pipeline inflation sits beside ECB caution; weak Japanese auction demand sits beside expectations of only gradual BOJ tightening; and Hungary can ease because prior currency strength changed its inflation path. This divergence prevents a single global duration impulse. For Treasuries, the relevant transmission is a high and uneven foreign clearing rate, which helps explain why the US long end lagged the front-end rally. Taiwan added a financial-stability constraint beneath its 2% policy rate. Margin borrowing for equities had increased 160% over 12 months, brokerages had issued nearly $1.2 billion of bonds during the year to fund working capital, and stock-trade defaults more than doubled in June to over NT$2 billion. The rush for leverage had even contributed to an undersubscribed central-bank debt auction on June 3. Defaults still represented less than 0.002% of transactions and none of 34 active brokerages had breached regulatory limits as of May, so the evidence did not establish a system break. It did show how an AI-led equity boom could redirect bank and broker balance sheets away from safer assets and transmit a sharp correction into household spending, funding costs and local bond demand.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market debt faced a firmer dollar even as US Treasury yields declined. EMB lost 0.1452%, while the US Dollar Index gained 0.3861% to 101.41. The mild fund decline suggests that lower benchmark yields provided some offset to tighter currency conditions, but it did not reproduce the high-grade benefit seen in LQD. Dollar strength remained the more difficult channel for external borrowers with weak reserves, large import bills or near-term refinancing needs.

Iran’s prospective access to frozen funds illustrated the difference between liquidity release and unrestricted financing. An Iranian official said $12 billion was poised to be released in 2 equal tranches, while the United States had not confirmed the amount. President Donald Trump said any released money could be used only for food and medical purchases from the United States. The arrangement could support essential imports, yet its restrictions would limit the funds’ flexibility for broader external obligations.

The same diplomatic process left a terms-of-trade uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz. Iran and Oman said they would begin work on an agreement governing the waterway and remained committed to keeping it secure and open. The possible cost of transit was still to be resolved, including concern that a toll could be introduced. Continued security would support oil normalization and importers’ external balances; a costly transit regime could preserve freight and energy pressure even without renewed military disruption.

Senegal supplied a more direct debt-management warning. A senior cabinet minister said the country was open to restructuring as mounting payment pressures threatened important economic sectors. No transaction terms were established, so the development marks willingness to consider liability relief rather than a completed restructuring. It nonetheless shows how sectoral stress can move a sovereign from routine financing toward negotiations over the timing and burden of repayment. Raizen supplied a corporate restructuring update with direct recovery implications. IG4 Capital said it had enough capital to buy debt entirely in cash while seeking a 50.1% equity stake after 45% of roughly 65 billion reais, or $12.8 billion, of debt converts into about 80% of the company. Creditors could receive cash, fund units or derivatives linked to a later sale, and IG4 had until March to accumulate claims. The proposal remained preliminary and the value split between businesses was undefined, but cash capacity made the control option more executable than a purely conditional bid.

These cases describe dispersion under a strong-dollar backdrop. Iran may receive narrowly usable external resources through diplomacy, whereas Senegal is considering a change to debt terms because payment pressure has become economically disruptive. The small decline in broad emerging-market debt masks that difference. Dollar liquidity is available on highly country-specific conditions, and sovereign outcomes depend on the legal use of funds, creditor terms and the domestic cost of maintaining external payments. Turkey showed the reward and fragility of high-carry access. Foreign-exchange carry positions rebuilt to about $30 billion and foreign holdings of local-currency bonds to roughly $15 billion, including at least $6 billion of carry inflows in the latest week. One- and 3-month implied lira yields fell to 32% and 35%, while the central bank was funding banks at 40% and was estimated to have bought about $9 billion of foreign exchange. The inflow rebuilt reserves and demand, but remained sensitive to geopolitical escalation or a premature decline in local funding rates.

Morocco used lower food inflation to extend a pause, holding at 2.25% as May inflation slowed to 1.2%, while stronger agriculture and infrastructure spending supported the fastest growth since 2021. The current-account deficit forecast nevertheless rose to 4% of GDP for 2026 and 3.8% for 2027, preserving an external-balance qualification. Brazil's June minutes supplied the opposite credibility problem: headline and underlying inflation were moving farther above the 3% target even after a 3rd 25-basis-point cut to 14.25%, and policymakers signaled that the easing calibration could change. Together, the cases separated policy room earned by disinflation from easing that risks outrunning the inflation forecast.

## Cross asset

Equities supplied the clearest haven impulse for Treasuries. The S&P 500 fell 1.4363%, the Nasdaq 100 dropped 3.2946% and the semiconductor index lost 7.8731%. The semiconductor decline followed an unusually strong run and left the index up 10.4894% over 1 month, making the session look like a concentrated unwind in AI leadership more than a uniform collapse in economic expectations. That concentration helps explain why the Treasury bid was strongest in policy-sensitive maturities.

Volatility rose, but remained short of disorderly levels. The VIX increased 12.7893% to 19.49. A move toward protection was consistent with lower Treasury yields and a stronger dollar, while the level did not signal a systemic funding event. SpaceX shares managed to recover after their earlier losses even as chipmakers sold off, another sign that the equity shock was large but uneven across the technology complex.

Oil reinforced the decline in inflation compensation. WTI fell 2.1518% to $73.21 and Brent declined 1.0526% to $77.08. Both contracts were down more than 24% over 1 month. The daily fall reduced the immediate energy input into headline inflation, and the longer decline strengthened the case for lower breakevens. Ongoing negotiations over Hormuz administration kept the durability of that relief conditional.

The dollar complicated a simple risk-off interpretation. The Dollar Index rose to 101.41, gaining 0.3861% on the day and 1.8786% over 1 week. Haven demand contributed, but the move also reflected the contrast between a still-hawkish Fed and more mixed policy prospects abroad. A front-end Treasury rally can therefore coexist with tighter dollar conditions when investors question the timing of the next hike without abandoning the relative US rate advantage.

Gold fell 1.2435% to $4,129.8999 despite the equity selloff. The metal was down 4.6411% over 1 week and 8.6507% over 1 month. Its weakness aligned with a stronger dollar and elevated real yields, indicating that the equity shock did not revive inflation or geopolitical hedging strongly enough to offset the opportunity cost of holding bullion.

Cross-asset markets therefore reinforced different parts of the fixed-income thesis. Equities and volatility generated demand for safety; crude supported lower breakevens; the dollar and gold showed that the real-rate and relative-policy regime remained restrictive. The combined message fits a Treasury bull steepening driven by policy timing and risk reduction, not a broad collapse in the expected path of nominal or real rates.

## Forward Market Significance

The June 25 U.S. data slate at 8:30 ET, led by May personal income and outlays, will determine whether the front-end rally can coexist with the post-FOMC real-rate reset. Core PCE prices rose 0.2% in April and headline PCE rose 0.4%, while spending increased 0.5% and income was unchanged; initial claims, durable-goods orders and the 3rd estimate of Q1 GDP are due at the same time. Softer underlying inflation, weaker spending momentum and additional labor-market cooling, especially with breakevens contained, would validate the June 23 reduction in urgency around the next Fed move and could extend relief from 2 through 10 years. A fresh acceleration in core-price breadth, resilient household demand or renewed supply-chain pressure would undermine that interpretation, lift real yields and reopen the possibility that Warsh’s more restrictive reaction function requires an earlier increase.

Supply moves to the belly on June 24, when Treasury sells $70 billion of 5-year notes at 13:00 ET after a $28 billion 2-year floating-rate reopening and a 119-day bill auction at 11:30. The June 25 sequence adds $44 billion of 7-year notes at 13:00 and paired 4- and 8-week bill sales at 11:30; the coupon securities settle June 30, keeping bidding separate from the later cash transfer. Strong bid-to-cover ratios, broad direct and indirect participation, contained dealer awards and stable cash-bill yields would extend the strong 2-year result and support the view that the belly can absorb government supply after the SpaceX hedge was removed. Weak 5- or 7-year demand, heavy dealer participation or renewed pressure in 5-year real yields would reopen a supply premium and challenge the orderly-funding interpretation that accompanied Tuesday’s rally.

The international clearing-rate test begins with Australia’s May CPI at 11:30 Sydney time on June 24, followed by Japan’s roughly ¥700 billion 20-year JGB reopening around 12:35 Tokyo time on June 25 and Banco de Mexico’s decision at 15:00 ET that day. Australia’s prior inflation readings were 0.4% monthly and 4.2% yearly, so softer breadth and a steadier currency would reduce pressure for another tightening step and lower the regional real-rate floor. Strong JGB coverage and firm end-user demand would temper the buyer-base concern created by the weak 5-year sale; a wider tail or softer coverage would intensify competition for global long duration. Banxico enters with a 6.50% policy rate. An unchanged decision accompanied by a stable peso would show that lower oil and policy credibility can contain the dollar channel, whereas renewed currency pressure or tighter guidance would reinforce the constraint from the stronger U.S. dollar and weaken the benign reading of the small EMB decline.

section_summaries.summary: A firmer dollar outweighed part of the Treasury rally for emerging-market debt, exposing country-specific liquidity constraints. Iran's prospective funds remained restricted to essential imports, while Senegal's openness to restructuring showed how payment pressure can shift a sovereign from routine financing toward liability relief.

section_summaries.market_read: Risk reduction supported Treasuries, but cross-asset conditions did not signal systemic stress.
section_summaries.next_check: The key check is whether equity weakness broadens beyond technology or remains a concentrated unwind.
section_summaries.summary: A concentrated semiconductor rout and higher volatility created a haven bid, while falling oil lowered inflation compensation. The stronger dollar and weaker gold confirmed that restrictive real-rate and relative-policy conditions endured, so the cross-asset signal favored policy-timing relief rather than a collapse in expected rates.

section_summaries.market_read: The thesis now depends on confirmation from inflation, supply absorption and foreign demand.

section_summaries.summary: 3 tests will determine whether front-end relief broadens: U.S. inflation and spending data, 5- and 7-year Treasury demand, and the international clearing rate across Australia, Japan and Mexico. Softer inflation and firm auctions would support duration, while renewed price or supply pressure would lift real yields.

overall_summary.headline: Front-end Treasury rally steepens the curve as oil and equity stress temper hike urgency
overall_summary.session_narrative: Policy-sensitive Treasuries led the rally after a semiconductor-led equity selloff, lower oil and a well-received 2-year auction eased the immediate inflation and supply premium. Lower breakevens carried the nominal long-end move even as real yields rose, showing that investors revised the timing of restraint more than its eventual extent. High-grade returns benefited from duration, but softer high-yield and EM debt, a firmer dollar and price-sensitive primary demand limited the easing signal.
overall_summary.summary: The June 23 NY close delivered a bull steepening as safety demand, cheaper crude and strong 2-year auction demand pulled policy-sensitive yields lower. The move reduced urgency around the next Fed increase but stopped short of a broad dovish reset because real yields stayed firm, activity remained resilient and credit absorption was selective.
